steps.title: Ingest 4,000 papers
steps.say: An invented research field: 20 interventions, 20 biomarkers, 20 outcomes, and twenty years of papers reporting on them with the usual noise. Each abstract is parsed for its findings, and each citation for whether it agrees, disagrees or just mentions.

steps.title: Pick a claim
steps.say: Search for papers on kallexjorib and serum traphenjorase, and take the finding from the top result.

steps.title: What supports it, and what contradicts it?
steps.say: Every other paper that tested the same pair, split by what it found and weighted by study design and sample size; then what later papers said when they cited this one.

steps.title: What does the supporting evidence rest on?
steps.say: A systematic-review table for the question: the verdict by study design and by period, and the datasets, methods and most-cited papers that carry it.

steps.title: Three hypotheses nobody has tested
steps.say: If A reliably moves B, and B reliably moves C, and no paper has ever tested A against C, that is a candidate. Each one comes with the papers behind both links, the weakest point in the argument, and a study that could prove it wrong.

steps.title: A claim with nothing solid to build on
steps.say: The same request for a finding whose concepts have no well-supported onward links. The gate holds: nothing is proposed rather than something weak.

steps.title: Were the hypotheses right?
steps.say: Only a simulation can answer this: the field was generated from a hidden cause-and-effect graph, so each hypothesis can be checked against it. Then the audit trail.
